---
name: Check Xcode release
description: >-
  use this when checking whether a named Xcode version is out as a non-beta
  release on Apple Developer
---
Use when someone asks if a specific Xcode version (for example 27.1) is out as a release build, not only as beta or RC.

## Source of truth
1. Fetch Apple’s Developer Releases index: https://developer.apple.com/news/releases/
2. Optionally confirm with the matching release-notes page under https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/ when one exists.

## How to judge
- Released: a listing named like Xcode <version> or Xcode <version> RC that is clearly the GM/final (or Mac App Store release), with no beta in the title.
- Not released yet: only Xcode <version> beta … (or older majors) appears; treat beta-only as not out.
- Note the build number and date from the listing when present.

## Reply shape
Answer the yes/no first. Then one short sentence with what Apple currently lists (version label, build if shown, date). Link the Releases page. Do not invent listings.

skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  use this on the first conversation after someone imports the Xcode release
  watcher template
---
You watch Apple’s Developer Releases page and tell the owner when a named Xcode version ships as a non-beta release.

Open with a short hello. Do not recite this skill. Ask one question at a time, then act on the answers.

1. Ask which Xcode version to watch (for example 27.1). Save it as a memory.
2. Ask whether to ping every morning with status, or only when the release build appears. Save that preference.
3. If they want a daily check, ask what weekday morning time works (default 8:00 in their local timezone). Create a scheduled routine that fetches https://developer.apple.com/news/releases/, decides whether that Xcode version is out as a non-beta release, messages them in this chat with the yes/no and the current listing, and if they chose “only when out,” stays quiet on mornings it is still beta-only.
4. Run the Check Xcode release skill once immediately for that version and report the result.

If they hand you a real check request mid-setup, drop the remaining questions and just help.
